epsilon_j_check.question: The Lean GridBound fixes the signs epsilon_j that the paper's Prop dyadic quantifies over. Does that mean the Lean does not certify the label's role?
epsilon_j_check.answer: No. The specialisation is the paper's own application instance, and it lives on the output side. The label's job, a majorant uniform over all modulations u, is fully present in GridBound and is discharged through the label lemmas.
evidence: Paper Prop dyadic (06-procedure.tex:10-47) quantifies over F_{j+1}-measurable epsilon_j with |epsilon_j| <= 1, 'the same epsilon_j for all modulations'. The procedure section (06-procedure.tex:55-66) says the coefficient is formed on the INPUT side and epsilon_j(x) only multiplies the OUTPUT, and 'the same multipliers are used for every piece and every label coordinate'. So the multipliers never enter the label construction.

The paper's only use of Prop dyadic is Thm good-set (11-fourier.tex:63-65): 'on the output side choose epsilon_j = r_{j+1}, so that g_I = r_{j+1} r_{j+2}'. A grep for prop:dyadic finds only the intro, the procedure statement, its proof in 09-assembly, and this application.

Lean: FinJump p F x = p.Gi(pos x) * p.avg(Hi * F) (Dyadic/Grid.lean:234). Gi = haarG o normarg, haarG x = haarH(2x) - haarH(2x-1) (Fourier/Haar.lean:18), and Gi_eq: Gi = L.Hi - R.Hi (Grid.lean:120). This is exactly the paper's summand E_p[rho chi_u h_I] * g_I with epsilon_j = r_{j+1}.

The fixed sign is consumed only in the output-path layer: Paths/Trip.lean (Gi_half, blow, trip_delay: blow x c = curl c.bit * curl d.bit; trip_final: |blow| = 1), Paths/Frost.lean last_lag (uses t^2 = k^2 and |blow| = 1), Paths/Letters.lean (proceeds/duties), Paths/Tilt.lean, Assembly/Rail.lean and Assembly/Cast.lean stage_shift. Grep finds NO use of Gi, haarG or blow in Thermal/ or Procedure/, where label, channel, fisher, bit_def, space_deficit and fisher_bound live.

The frequency supremum is intact. GridBound has 'exists W ... forall x good, forall u : Grid M, ||FinShift J (finMod rho u) x|| <= W x' with expU W <= C 2^j, i.e. one majorant for all 2^M modulations, uniformly as M -> infinity.

The label lemmas are on the comparator chain (extract_lean BFS): paperMain -> almost_everywhere_fourier_convergence -> gridProof -> grossOur -> upper_total -> Road.fisher_bound -> one_split_price -> space_deficit -> bit_def, with fisher_bound -> Thermal.channel -> Thermal.label. Separately: gridProof -> annual_valid -> gala -> main_stage -> ride -> below_decode -> decode_track -> gain_decode -> duet_decode. And: gridProof -> plant -> fund_est -> certified_add -> F_increment -> cred_mono -> cred_add_mono -> ginibre. Thermal.label has 323 dependents in the DAG (24% of 2014 declarations).
epsilon_j_check.residual_caveat: The Lean does NOT certify the general-multiplier Prop dyadic. Downstream targets that need other output multipliers would need the general form: variational Carleson, other Haar kernels, Walsh variants whose output signs are not r_{j+1} r_{j+2}. The fix looks local: replace curl c.bit by an arbitrary depth-(j+1)-measurable epsilon with |epsilon| <= 1 in trip_delay, trip_final and last_lag, using t^2 <= k^2 instead of equality, and complex parts in Frost. The extra lines (perhaps 100-300) are a guess from reading these four files, not a measurement.
epsilon_j_check.recommended_check: State GeneralGridBound (epsilon : N -> Grid M -> C, constant on depth-(j+1) blocks, ||epsilon|| <= 1, FinJump with epsilon j * r_{j+2} in place of Gi). This is statable now in about 25 lines from Dyadic/Grid.lean. Then verify that the proof changes are confined to Paths/ and Assembly/Cast. Doing so would close the issue formally.
epsilon_j_check.verdict: The specialisation does not undercut the label. Remove the 'Lean may not certify the label's step' caveat from the shortlist and replace it with 'Lean certifies the epsilon_j = r_{j+1} instance (the one the paper uses); general multipliers are unformalised and are output-side only'.

lean_source.name: OAI.FourierLLogL.Dyadic.Thermal.Form
lean_source.text:
/-- coefficient form. Throughout, nonnegativity of the coefficients means `0 ≤ A`. -/
abbrev Form (M : ℕ) := Grid M → ℝ

lean_source.name: Thermal.wave / cost / form
lean_source.text:
def wave (s y : Grid M) : ℝ := (chi s y).re
def cost (s y : Grid M) : ℝ := 1-wave s y
def form (A : Form M) : Grid M → ℝ := fun y => ∑ s, A s * cost s y

lean_source.name: Thermal.boltz / q
lean_source.text:
def boltz (A : Form M) (y : Grid M) : ℝ := exp (-form A y)
def q (A : Form M) (u : Grid M) : ℝ := (fc (fun y => (↑(boltz A y):ℂ)) u).re

lean_source.name: Thermal.F / K (free energy, label density K_A = e^{F-A})
lean_source.text:
def F (A : Form M) := -log (q A 0)
def K (A : Form M) (x : Grid M) : ℝ := boltz A x / q A 0

lean_source.name: Thermal.label (noise law theta ~ K_A)
lean_source.text:
/-- Label noise law centered at zero relative to counting measure. -/
def label (A : Form M) : Law (Grid M) :=
  ⟨fun x => side M * K A x, fun x => mul_nonneg (side_pos _).le (K_pos _ _).le, by
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum]
    exact K_total _⟩

lean_source.name: Thermal.cred (thermal Fourier coefficient c_A(u) = int chi_u K_A)
lean_source.text: def cred (A : Form M) (u : Grid M) := q A u/q A 0

lean_source.name: Thermal.delta (metric Delta_A)
lean_source.text: def delta (A : Form M) (s : Grid M) := √((label A).Ex fun i => ‖1-chi s i‖^2)

lean_source.name: Thermal.channel (the label Z = Y + theta)
Thermal.omegaObs / Mz / fz (label-weighted masses M(z) and moments f(z))
Thermal.S (spatial form S_p = R^2 (1 - Re chi_1))
lean_source.text:
/-- Spatial form, specified by inverse width -/
def S (M : ℕ) (R : ℝ) : Form M := fun s => if s=1 then R^2 else 0

lean_source.name: Thermal.place
lean_source.text: def place (p : Node) (M : ℕ) := S M p.invlen

lean_source.name: Thermal.Update.next (label update A+ = A + S_p + D_i)
lean_source.text: def next (u : Update j M p) (A : Form M) : Form M := A+place p M+u.changeForm

lean_source.name: Procedure.Fund.advance (main channel 'mood' replaced by u.next)
lean_source.text:
def advance (p : Node) (c : Fund M) (u : Update j M p) : Fund M :=
    ⟨u.next c.mood,p,c.uses+1,c.spend+u.credit,c.bank+u.bill⟩

lean_source.name: Procedure.hist / diff / fisher (J_p = sum |D|^2/M)
Procedure.givenD / massInfo (per-node label Fisher charge)
Thermal.ginibre (key lemma: Griffiths-Ginibre covariance positivity)
lean_source.text:
theorem ginibre {A : Form M} (hA : 0 ≤ A) (s t : Grid M) :
    cred A s * cred A t ≤ (label A).Ex (fun i => wave s i * wave t i)

lean_source.name: Procedure.bit_def (key lemma: Fisher information of label <= 4 x bit relative-entropy deficit)
lean_source.text:
lemma bit_def (s : Scene M) (k : Grid M → Law α) (hp : s.here.valid)
    (he : s.here.lev < M) (hh : 0 ≤ s.wage) (hm : 0 < s.mass) (hn : 0 < s.norm) :
    s.norm/s.mass * fisher s k ≤ 4*(log 2-sideH (step s) k)

lean_source.name: Procedure.space_deficit (key lemma: one-step chain-rule identity charging the Fisher term to the entropy deficit)
lean_source.text:
lemma space_deficit (s : Scene M) (k : Grid M → Law α) (hp : s.here.valid)
    (he : s.here.lev < M) (hh : 0 ≤ s.wage) (hm : 0 < s.mass) (hn : 0 < s.norm) :
    (step s).probs.Ex (fun b => deficit (s.smaller b) k) +
      (1/4:ℝ)*(s.norm/s.mass)*fisher s k ≤ deficit s k

lean_source.name: Procedure.Road.fisher_bound (key lemma: global label Fisher sum <= limitC * height j, i.e. O(d))
lean_source.text:
lemma fisher_bound :
    ∀ᶠ j : ℕ in atTop, ∀ M J : ℕ, ∀ f : Grid M → ℝ,
      (∀ x, f x ≤ exp (height j)) →
      let s := beginPlay f true
      ∀ t : Road j M s, Trusted J f t → 1/Thermal.H j ≤ s.mass →
        t.flatFee infoFee ≤ limitC* height j

lean_source.name: Procedure.Paths.Troupe.duet_decode (key lemma: exact decoding identity int chi_k a^v = c_A(k) * scalar(v+k))
lean_source.text:
lemma duet_decode (s : Scene M) (v k : Grid M) :
    ∑ z, chi k z*letter s v z = (cred (dye s) k:ℂ)*scalar s (v+k)

lean_source.name: Procedure.Paths.Troupe.energy_near_channel (label energy of v controlled by that of v+k plus Delta_A(k)^2)
lean_source.text:
lemma energy_near_channel (s : Scene M) (h : Fit s) (v k : Grid M) :
    energy s v ≤ 2*energy s (v+k)+2*(share s*delta (dye s) k^2)

lean_source.name: Dyadic.GridBound
lean_source.kind: def (Lean's version of Prop dyadic: sup over ALL u, u-independent majorant W)
lean_source.text:
/-- Finite cut statement; asks for an L¹ majorant restricted to points where density steps stay
below threshold. There is no dependence on a frequency or depth cutoff in the constant. -/
def GridBound : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ᶠ j : ℕ in atTop, ∀ J : ℕ, ∀ᶠ M : ℕ in atTop,
    ∀ (ρ : Grid M → ℝ), (∀ x, 0 ≤ ρ x) → expU ρ ≤ 2 →
      (∀ x, ρ x ≤ Real.exp ((2:ℝ)^j)) →
    ∃ W : Grid M → ℝ, (∀ x, 0 ≤ W x) ∧ expU W ≤ C*(2:ℝ)^j ∧
      ∀ x : Grid M, finGood (((j:ℝ)+1)^3) J ρ x →
        ∀ u : Grid M, ‖FinShift J (finMod ρ u) x‖ ≤ W x
lean_source.note: added in downstream pass (verbatim, proof cut at :=)

theorem_corollaries: Carleson's theorem (L^2), since L^2 is inside L log L on the circle. With paperMain in L it is about 5 lines; it must be EXCLUDED from any speedup measurement, or L must omit paperMain/gridProof. F1 listed it as a speedup target; it is moved here.
Kolmogorov-Seliverstov-Plessner (its hypothesis gives f in L^2). Moved here from the F1 speedup list for the same reason.
Hunt's theorem in L^p, p > 1; Sjolin's L log L log log L; Antonov's L log L log log log L (trigonometric): all contained in L log L.
Weak-L^1 maximal bound on L log L (already in Lean: Main.lean weak_L1_maximal_bound) and maximal_good_sets.
The gap in Konyagin's optimal-Orlicz-class problem shrinks to between the divergence class and L log L.

release_reuse.text: No other family in the release uses thermal labels, the label-update rule, or the two-law Fisher-sum identity (grep over all preprint .tex for 'Ginibre', 'noisy label', 'noisy observation', 'thermal form', 'Fisher sum', 'label character'; Ginibre hits elsewhere are ordinary stat-mech uses in Ising/XY/O(n) papers). Closest sibling device: family 093 (dimension-free log-Sobolev for subgaussian log-concave measures, 01-introduction.tex:166-178) predicts w(Y) from a noisy observation Y + sqrt(r) G with repeated Gaussian observations and entropy-loss accounting - the same 'noisy side-channel + entropy budget' pattern but with standard Gaussian noise, no decoding of characters, no adaptive tightening; it is in the stochastic-localization tradition. Families that could use the device: 083 (Hilbert transform along Lipschitz directions; uses Lacey-Thiele tiles for the Carleson-along-lines input, 03-ordinary-tiles.tex:6), 082 (maximal/variational triangular Hilbert transform, time-frequency), 154 (pointwise multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations), 080 (Schrodinger maximal estimates). None of them currently uses it; only 083 has a clear Carleson-operator sub-step where it could slot in.
release_reuse.lean_notes_2026_10_09: 075 imports OAI/Analysis/Fourier (HeightLayers, SphereExtension; symmetricPartialSum). The ExactFourier and UniformFourier comparators belong to Computability families and are unrelated. No other OAI directory uses Thermal.label, the channel or the Fisher lemmas.

negative_controls.why_device_must_fail: A proved-false analogue: the device must not 'prove' a.e. convergence in L^1. Budgets scale with d = log ||rho||_inf and are unbounded for L^1 densities. A prover that derives L^1 convergence from the label lemmas has a broken library.

top5.target: O1: Walsh GridBound (finite Walsh L log L)
top5.argument: This is the cheapest and most decisive Lean check, and the shortlist's own 'run first' test. The statement is about 30-60 new lines on top of Dyadic/Grid.lean. The obstruction is identical. Decoding becomes exactly multiplicative, the output-side Haar sign structure is the same one GridBound already fixes (so the epsilon_j specialisation is no obstacle), and the Fisher lemmas are channel-agnostic. The formal baseline is gridProof's 2014-declaration DAG minus the Fourier transfer layer. A successful port shows the device is portable. A sceptic will call it 'the same theorem on another group', so it confirms portability, not a jump.

top5.target: S2 / O2: Bourgain's multi-frequency lemma, finite dyadic model
top5.argument: This is the only DIFFERENT theorem where the obstruction (a loss in the number of frequencies) is the whole difficulty. The statement takes about 30-50 new lines using OAI's chi, Node.avg and expU. Any frequency-count saving would be a speedup on a 35-year-old theorem and would confirm the item. I rate it low-medium because of two real mismatches: the label budget is entropy (L log L), while Bourgain is L^2; and Bourgain's operator sums over theta inside the absolute value, while GridBound takes a sup over one modulation. Also check that the rough dyadic-average variant has a known (log N)^2 bound before using it.

top5.target: S1: Walsh-Carleson theorem via the label route
top5.argument: This is a known theorem with a tile proof of about 20-30 pp. and no formalisation. It is statable in under 300 lines (Walsh-Paley functions on [0,1)). If O1 works it becomes a corollary. If O1 stalls, an L^2-only version measures whether the label lemmas shorten a tile-free proof.

top5.target: S3: Walsh L log L log log log L (Sjolin-Soria)
top5.argument: This is a known Walsh theorem strictly weaker than O1. As a speedup target it compares the label route against extrapolation from weak-L^p Walsh-Carleson bounds. It is statable in under 300 lines and shares definitions with S1.

top5.target: O3: Variational Carleson in L log L
top5.argument: This is likely new and the Fisher budget is unchanged. It is statable in under 300 lines with OAI's symmetricPartialSum. It is the target that most needs the GENERAL-multiplier Prop dyadic, so it doubles as the test of whether the epsilon_j specialisation costs anything downstream. It is in the same family of problems, so it is weaker evidence than S2.

precedent_check.text: No earlier equivalent of the full device (noisy label of the input point with ferromagnetic thermal noise, adaptive tightening A+ = A + S_p + D_i, two-law Fisher sum, exact character decoding) was found in harmonic analysis: searches for information-theoretic / noisy-observation proofs of Carleson-type theorems returned only tile-based proofs (Carleson, Fefferman, Lacey-Thiele, Lie, Di Plinio) and the 2026 Lean formalisation of Carleson's theorem. However, every ingredient has a precedent: (i) the noise law K_A is a centred generalised von Mises distribution (Maksimov 1967; Gatto-Jammalamadaka 2007) = one-site plane-rotator Gibbs measure; its covariance positivity is Ginibre 1970 (cited); (ii) 'observe a hidden variable through progressively less noisy channels and bound the total information by the entropy via the chain rule' is stochastic localization in its information-theoretic form (Eldan; El Alaoui-Montanari arXiv:2109.00709, where the I-MMSE/chain-rule identity bounds the integrated estimation error by the entropy) and the pinning lemma (Montanari 2008; Raghavendra-Tan 2012), already noted as an uncited precedent for item I12; (iii) 'sum over scales of squared conditional biases <= relative entropy via chain rule + Pinsker' is Tao's entropy-decrement method (arXiv:1509.05422; Tao-Teravainen arXiv:1710.02112) and the folklore dyadic entropy bound; (iv) 'cost of an adaptively selected statistic is paid by mutual information rather than by a union bound over the statistics' is Russo-Zou (arXiv:1511.05219) / information-theoretic generalisation bounds, and noise injection to limit information is the Gaussian mechanism of differential privacy; (v) recovering characters from a positive-definite smoothing kernel with coefficient close to 1 on a metric ball is the Bohr-set / large-spectrum duality of additive combinatorics. Verdict: the combination (a label whose information is charged under the input law, whose decoding is exact and frequency-count-free, and whose noise is tightened adaptively with a free-energy/packing potential) has no equivalent found; the abstract mechanism is a cross-field transfer of stochastic-localization / information-budget ideas into Carleson theory. Recommend keeping N3 provisionally but flag a real N2 risk (transfer of the stochastic-localization template). Post-release (after Oct 6, 2026): no paper, blog or forum post found that uses or discusses the device; press coverage only lists family 075 by title; the release's history.md has no entry for 075.
precedent_check.update_2026_10_09_downstream: No new web search in this pass: the brief allowed reuse, and WebFetch hit a session limit. The F1 verdict stands: no earlier equivalent of the full device; every ingredient is precedented (generalised von Mises / Ginibre, stochastic localization, Tao's entropy decrement, Russo-Zou); real N2 risk. No post-Oct-6 use was found in the F1 search.
